findings.title: Development Approach miscounts the `_inject_file_contents` call sites / direct callers
findings.description: Step 2 says: "Update its two `review_client` call sites and the direct callers in `test_content_injection.py`, `test_convention_root.py`, `test_injection_decision.py`, and `test_review_client.py`." Against the current source this is slightly off: there is **one** production call site of `_inject_file_contents` (`review_client.py:154` inside `run_review_with_profile`), not two; and `test_injection_decision.py` and `test_review_client.py` are **not** direct callers — the former exercises the return only via `run_review_with_profile`, and the latter merely patches the symbol (`tests/review/test_review_client.py:224`, `side_effect=lambda p, *a, **k: p`). Only `test_content_injection.py` and `test_convention_root.py` invoke it directly. This slightly misstates the mechanical blast radius of the `(prompt, DiffInjection | None)` return-type change, but it is trivially self-correcting (an implementer's grep finds the true call sites, and the over-listed files simply need no change), so it does not leave a stated requirement unmet. Worth correcting for plan accuracy only.

findings.title: Design aligns with the slice plan and 900 architecture scope
findings.description: For the record: no scope was dropped or deferred that the slice plan entry (927) assigns to this slice — Parts A/B/C are all delivered, and the items deferred (#137 ordering/`--stat`, #138 file-body truncation, #114, `max_file_size_bytes` default change) are the exact items the plan marks "not in scope" or routes to issues via its own "otherwise it becomes an issue" clause. The verdict-capping rule and the answering-model record are presented as run-integrity facts consistent with the 916–920 artifact-trust lineage, not as a new gated capability, so they remain within the maintenance initiative's boundary.
